title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Personal and fitness training
audience: Personal trainers and fitness coaches, including solo trainers, who want to charge more for packages, programmes and workplace sessions.
learningOutcomes: Write a training offer with a measurable outcome you control, a time frame and clear conditions
Identify the booking, cancellation and prepayment friction a client carries, and reduce it
Price the offer on value, then check it against your hours, costs and insurance

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'One PT session, $X' is a price for a service. 'A 12-week plan: a written starting check, sessions at fixed times, a home log we review together, and a measured re-check at weeks 6 and 12' is an offer. The client buys a visible programme and the confidence that someone will track it. Do not promise body-composition, strength or health results you cannot guarantee. Promise the process you control and the measurements you will take.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: Name the outcome you control, such as the sessions delivered and the measured reviews completed. Set a time frame that matches the programme. Name the work the client must do, such as attending booked times and keeping a home log. Give certainty through a written plan, session notes and a sign-off at each review. State the risk you carry, such as a make-up session when you cancel, backed by the professional indemnity and public liability cover you hold. Put the scope and exclusions in writing. A written quote can become binding once it is accepted, and the exclusions should name what sits outside the programme, such as medical advice or treatment (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction, prepayment and direct debit
instruction.body: Trainers often lose clients to booking and cancellation hassle rather than to price. Use one booking route, one reschedule window and one written cancellation rule. Direct debit is common in this trade. NSW Fair Trading says direct debits often need 30 days' written notice to stop, so put the stop process in writing before the first debit (NSW Fair Trading, last updated 15 April 2026). Queensland guidance for gym and fitness providers asks for a plain-English fee statement before signing. It also limits prepayment: it may not run more than 12 months ahead, and prepaid money is refunded within 14 days, less services used and any disclosed admin fee (Queensland Government, last updated 23 July 2024). The Queensland scope is 'gym or fitness provider', and whether it covers a sole personal trainer needs checking. For NSW, a 2015 news report said the government would cancel the Fitness Services (Pre-paid Fees) Act 2000. The report does not confirm that the change took effect, so this lesson does not treat it as settled. Check NSW Fair Trading before you sell prepaid blocks in NSW.

instruction.heading: Guarantees, cancellation rights and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford, such as a make-up session for one you cancel. Consumer guarantees apply to services, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a client's rights for services (business.gov.au, Warranties and refunds, 27 May 2025). A written workmanship-style warranty can sit on top of those rights, but it cannot replace them. Western Australia's fitness code of practice names personal trainers and yoga classes. It says cancellation by email is enough, that cancellation can take effect up to 30 days after notice, and that new memberships carry up to a 7-day cooling-off. The page does not say whether the code is mandatory, so verify that before you rely on it (WA Consumer Protection, published and updated 2 April 2025). Publish only results you have measured, with the client's written consent, and check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measured claim.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, then check the price against cost and time. Council prices give a reference point for what clients already compare. City of Sydney Leisure lists a 30-minute single session at $71 and a six-session pack at $348.40. It lists a 60-minute single session at $112.60 and a ten-session pack at $923.80 (City of Sydney Leisure, page date not shown, fetched 9 November 2026). This is one council's public list, run by a council with its own cost base. It is not a market rate for a sole trainer. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin, so test each package against cost before you decide on any premium (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes, 1 August 2025). Show one clear total and say whether GST is included, as Western Australia's guidance asks (WA Consumer Protection, updated 4 September 2026). That guidance also says a deposit should generally be no more than 10 per cent of the price, with later payments tied to completed stages. Stepped packages, where each higher level adds something visible such as a check-in or a home programme, are one way to present the options (Jobber Academy, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). The Jobber article predates 2022, so use it for the method only.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a client would repeat, using only things you can measure and control.
Set a time frame you can keep, and record how often you meet it.
List what the client must do, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a written plan, session notes or a measured review.
Decide the make-up and cancellation terms, and check that you can afford them.
Price from value, then check the rate against cost, time and insurance.

workedExamples.situation: A personal trainer charges by the session. Clients who ask about a 12-week goal say they cannot tell what they will get for the money, and two have left after the first month.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer, decide its structure and set what the client pays for.
workedExamples.reasoning: A fixed 12-week package with a written starting check, a booked session pattern, two measured reviews and a make-up rule for sessions you cancel gives the client something checkable. Price the package from your own hours, costs and insurance, then compare it with a council's public price list rather than copying it. Put the direct debit stop process in writing, and check any prepayment against your state's rules before you sell it.

commonErrors.error: Making a guarantee you cannot afford to honour
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the guarantee to something you control, such as a make-up session.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate
commonErrors.prevention: Publish only results you have measured, with the client's written consent, and check current ACCC guidance first.

commonErrors.error: Selling prepaid blocks beyond your state's prepayment limits
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state rule before you sell. In Queensland, prepayment may not run more than 12 months ahead.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business and consumer guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Better Health says industry registration is optional for personal trainers. Check your state's rules and your insurer's terms before acting.

Prepaid packages and cancellation rules differ by state. The NSW prepayment law is unverified: a 2015 news report announced its cancellation, and no source here confirms the outcome. Check NSW Fair Trading before relying on any NSW rule. The WA fitness code names personal trainers, but the page does not state whether it is mandatory.
Health claims: this lesson does not set a health-screening standard, because none was verified in the research. Do not promise health or body-change outcomes in any offer.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost, time and insurance.
Every measured claim is backed by the client's own measured results and the client's written consent.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or package terms with scope, exclusions, cancellation rule and prepayment terms
Pricing check showing cost, hours, insurance and the decision made
summary: A good offer promises a measurable outcome you control, with a time frame, certainty and a fair cancellation rule.
Direct debit, prepayment and cancellation rules differ by state, and the NSW prepayment law is unverified here.
Higher rates follow from clearer value, not from longer hours.

officialReferences.title: Prepare quotes (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: States that a written quote becomes binding once accepted and that a quote should recover cost plus a margin. Publisher: business.gov.au.

officialReferences.title: Warranties and refunds (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: Says an optional written warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees, and that a 'no refunds' line does not override rights for services. Publisher: business.gov.au.

officialReferences.title: Setting prices: what's allowed (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: States that misleading statements about prices are prohibited. Publisher: ACCC.

officialReferences.title: Estimates, quotes and deposits (WA Consumer Protection)
officialReferences.covers: Western Australia only. Asks for the total including GST and whether GST is included, and gives a deposit guideline of generally no more than 10 per cent. Publisher: WA Consumer Protection.

officialReferences.title: Fitness Industry Code of Practice: cancelling a gym membership (WA Consumer Protection)
officialReferences.covers: Says the code covers personal trainers and yoga classes, and sets out cancellation by email, the 30-day effect of notice and the 7-day cooling-off. Does not say whether the code is mandatory. Publisher: WA Consumer Protection.

officialReferences.title: Gym and fitness memberships (NSW Fair Trading)
officialReferences.covers: Says direct debits often need 30 days' written notice to stop, that unfair terms are void in standard-form contracts, and that consumer guarantees apply. States no prepayment cap. Publisher: NSW Fair Trading.

officialReferences.title: Join a gym or fitness provider (Queensland Government)
officialReferences.covers: Sets out a 48-hour cooling-off, prepayment limits of up to 12 months ahead, refunds within 14 days less services used, and a plain-English fee statement. Scope is 'gym or fitness provider'; coverage of sole trainers needs checking. Publisher: Queensland Government.
